name: dark-baseline-r1
context:
GAME THREE, DARKMATTER. A BASELINE DESIGN, ITS MONTE CARLO PROOF, AND THE PROOF'S FAILURE. The requirement placed on this work is that the baseline be BOTH proven by simulation AND independently audited before it is accepted as valid. The simulation has run and it FAILED. This brief therefore asks you to audit a design together with the evidence that it does not yet work, rather than a design presented as finished.

═══════════ WHAT THE GAME IS ═══════════

A seeded gravitational n-body universe, rebuilt from a seed every round, integrated in Q32.32 fixed point with velocity Verlet so it replays bitwise. The player perturbs a running system and the consequence arrives later through dynamics they did not author. Games one (dice, push-your-luck) and two (molecular synthesis on a grid) are turn-taking games on a static substrate; this one's substrate runs on its own.

The goal of this increment was to make it CONCEPTUALLY STRAIGHTFORWARD -- statable in one sentence a player acts on correctly, the way games one and two are.

═══════════ WHAT WAS MEASURED, AND THE RETRACTION IT FORCED ═══════════

M1 DECISION LEGIBILITY. Twelve mass drops around a ring; truth is the score after 360 steps. The best rule a human could execute from a still frame ranked the actions at Spearman 0.156. The RANDOM negative control read 0.076. The sampling noise of a Spearman over twelve points at these sample sizes is about 0.30. Two of five seeds produced ZERO outcome variance -- twelve different interventions, one identical score. The player cannot tell a good action from a bad one.

M2 A RETRACTION. The previous increment published 'timing is worth three times more than which verb you use' from two numbers (0.1464 for splitting one verb in time, 0.1949 for splitting across two verbs) in a novel-distance metric whose null had never been measured. It has now been measured on the identical harness, so the observed values reproduce exactly. The null is a point whose true novelty is ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION: one verb, one application, at a parameter value BETWEEN the reference grid's levels, hence inside the single-verb reachable set by definition. That null reads 0.1480. So 0.1464 is 0.99x the floor and 0.1949 is 1.32x it. Both effects are the ruler. The finding is withdrawn.

An earlier draft of that null was itself degenerate -- it drew the comparison point FROM the reference set, so its distance was exactly zero and the null could never fail -- and was caught before it ran.

M4 VERBS AND COST. Six verbs swept, with a price attached to each for the first time. Best equilibrium score: mass injection 0.529, angular-momentum torque 0.495, remove-a-body 0.375, phase shift 0.019, linear impulse 0.005, split-a-body 0.000. Under a budget, REMOVE drops from 0.375 to 0.000 because its flat price exceeds the cap. A verb that is good only when free is a cheat code, and this is the first measurement that could distinguish the two.

M5 BRANCHING. 2.7 live moves out of 20 and 2.63 bits of move-value entropy, against game two's 14.2 and 5.23.

═══════════ THE FALSIFICATION, WHICH BROKE THE CLAIM ═══════════

CLAIM: 'Darkmatter is illegible because its objective is a statistic of the whole system. Make it a NAMED BODY reaching a NAMED PLACE and the player can rank actions without understanding the physics.' The structural analogy was pool -- a continuous-control physics game with real chaotic sensitivity that novices play competently on their first afternoon, because the objective is a noun reaching a noun, the player acts once and then watches, and the table comes to rest.

Measured over nine seeds at three scene sizes, each objective scored against ITS OWN human rule:

  12 bodies, inertia band: 0 of 9 seeds live, best score 0.000
  12 bodies, noun target:  legibility -0.176 against a random control of +0.080, 9 of 9 live
   6 bodies, inertia band: legibility 0.296 vs 0.103, 4 of 9 live
   3 bodies, inertia band: legibility 0.196 vs -0.115, 7 of 9 live

The claim is FALSIFIED and not as predicted. The predicted failure was triviality -- legible because only one answer exists. What happened is that the noun objective's own human rule read NEGATIVE: aiming at the target is worse than guessing. What the noun objective did fix is RESPONSIVENESS (9/9 live against 0/9), not legibility. A single mass drop cannot move a twelve-body system's second moment by a quarter, so the band was not difficult, it was unreachable, and that had been read as difficulty.

One number in that table is the author's rather than the game's, and is reported as such: 'live moves 1.0' for the noun objective is an artifact of placing the zone at the landing of the furthest action, which guarantees exactly one action scores 1.000.

═══════════ THE MECHANISM, MEASURED RATHER THAN INFERRED ═══════════

'The heuristic reads negative' is equally consistent with having wired the heuristic backwards, so the angle between the bearing of the drop (as seen from the body) and the body's actual displacement was measured directly:

  horizon 30 steps  -> mean angle  2.2 deg, 100.0% within 45 deg, displacement 0.015
  horizon 60        -> mean angle  5.0 deg,  98.1% within 45 deg, displacement 0.067
  horizon 120       -> mean angle 12.2 deg,  95.4% within 45 deg, displacement 0.276
  horizon 240       -> mean angle 29.3 deg,  81.5% within 45 deg, displacement 0.850
  horizon 360       -> mean angle 41.0 deg,  67.6% within 45 deg, displacement 1.632
  horizon 600       -> mean angle 59.2 deg,  42.6% within 45 deg, displacement 3.381

The negative control fires at the top of the table: at a short horizon intuition is exactly right. So the heuristic is not wired backwards; it is correct, and it DECAYS WITH THE HORIZON. Everything had been scored at 360.

Torque was measured the same way and is perfectly monotone -- mean cluster radius 6.335, 6.997, 7.683, 8.386, 9.104, 9.827 across its sweep, no reversal. 'More spin, more spread' is exactly intuitive.

CORRECTED CLAIM (both versions kept): 'Darkmatter is illegible because it is measured at a horizon where intuition has decayed. The DIRECTION of a mass drop's effect is intuitive -- 95% correct within 45 degrees out to 120 steps -- and the MAGNITUDE never is. The objective was not the problem; the horizon was.'

That also splits the verbs by character: mass injection is a decision that is not rankable, torque is rankable but is a monotone dial. Neither alone is a game.

═══════════ THE BASELINE ═══════════

One sentence: 'Drop a mass, or spin the cluster, to steer the marked body into the marked ring before your budget runs out.'

  OBJECTIVE  a named body reaching a named place
  SCENE      5 bodies, one marked
  LATTICE    12 bearings x 2 verbs = 14 named actions, no continuous dial
  COST       per-verb prices against a round budget
  HORIZON    120 steps per shot, not 360
  REST       the score locks when the body crosses the ring
  FORECAST   an uncertainty cone at the measured Lyapunov exponent 0.098, computed from the search's own rollouts
  VERBS      mass + torque, with remove priced as the big swing

HORIZON displaced TEMPO from the factor list because the measurement said so.

═══════════ THE PROOF, WHICH FAILED ═══════════

Seven gates were written before the run. Twenty-four seeds, fourteen actions, four horizons. The target zone was placed BLIND to which action wins -- a bearing drawn from the seed, at the median displacement distance -- and a seed was served only if at least two actions reached it and doing nothing did not.

  horizon  legibility  its floor  served  live moves  entropy  agency  cost bite
       60       0.369      0.537    3/24         1.0     2.33   0.740       100%
      120       0.300      0.533    3/24         1.0     2.32   0.748       100%
      240       0.557      0.087    1/24         3.0     2.71   0.582       100%
      360      -0.079      0.425    4/24         1.3     2.17   0.832        50%

  G1 legibility clears its own floor by 1.5x      FAIL   0.300 vs floor 0.533
  G2 legibility RISES as the horizon falls        PASS   120: 0.300 / 360: -0.079
  G3 at least 70% of seeds served                 FAIL   3/24, an 87.5% rejection rate
  G4 at least 3 live moves of 14                  FAIL   1.0
  G5 entropy at least 2.0 bits                    PASS   2.32
  G6 agency over doing nothing at least 0.30      PASS   0.748
  G7 cost changes the answer on 30%+ of seeds     PASS   100%

BASELINE NOT PROVEN. Nothing was re-tuned to reach a pass.

The author's reading, which is exactly what wants auditing: G2 passing is the round's claim surviving. G1's floor of 0.533 is the random control over three samples -- a random ranking of fourteen actions on three seeds is noise of that size -- so G1 may be reporting that the experiment is too small rather than that legibility is absent. G4's 1.0 likewise rests on three seeds. And G3 is the cause of the small sample. The pre-registered rule for an 87.5% rejection rate is that the GENERATOR is declared defective and fixed rather than filtered.

A coverage measurement was run to separate two candidate causes: that the generator emits degenerate universes, or that ONE SHOT CANNOT AIM -- fourteen discrete actions reach fourteen places, so a target anywhere else is unreachable however good the universe is. With one shot the fourteen actions produce 10.8 distinct landings and cover 33.7% of the target annulus, with a median nearest-miss of 0.72 median displacements. With TWO shots separated in time they produce 48.3 distinct landings and cover 64.1%, and the median nearest-miss halves to 0.388. The generator is innocent: ONE SHOT CANNOT AIM.

That also revives, on a different metric, the idea the retraction above killed. The Lie-algebra import claimed composed verbs reach states neither reaches alone, and the novel-distance metric could not support it once its floor was measured. COVERAGE is a different estimator asking a different question -- not 'is the composed point far from the single-verb set' but 'how much of the target space can be hit at all' -- and on that one composition is worth 4.5x the distinct landings. Whether that is a rescue or a second bite at the same cherry is part of what wants auditing.

═══════════ THE ENGINE BUILT FOR THIS ═══════════

Game two's harness enumerates legal moves and beams over clonable state, which works because its move set is finite and small. A placement on a disc crossed with a real magnitude is neither. ORRERY: progressive widening for the continuous action space; common random numbers, antithetic universes (exact in fixed point, since negation is an integer sign flip) and successive-halving racing for variance; a prefix cache and a transposition table keyed on the exact Q32.32 digest (worthless in floating point, exact here) for cost; rollout depth capped at the MEASURED Lyapunov horizon of 204 steps rather than a chosen number; a do-nothing arm built into every evaluation; the forecast cone computed as a by-product of the search's own rollouts so the interface and the engine cannot drift apart; and a resolution-floor service that REFUSES a null scoring exactly zero, because that is the signature of a control drawn from the set it is measured against.

Its organising constraint: THERE IS EXACTLY ONE ACTION LATTICE, shared by the engine, the ceiling, the agents and the shipped interface. If the search discretises to twelve bearings while the player gets a continuous dial, the player can express actions the ceiling cannot and the ceiling is not a ceiling. Twenty-four oracles, each with a negative control seen to fail, are green.

═══════════ THE CANDIDATE COUNT, DERIVED ═══════════

Forty candidates, and the number is derived rather than chosen. 605 ms per play, measured before sizing anything. A cell needs about nine seeds to resolve a legibility difference of 0.2 against a Spearman noise of 0.30, so a cell is 117 plays or 71 seconds; a four-hour screening budget is therefore about 203 cells, and a resolution-V two-level design at 2^(k-1) cells can carry eight factors. Eight questions x four competing answers = 32 testable candidates, plus eight tail candidates the design cannot carry as levels and which are kept unpruned because trimming the tail to what is screenable is the judge reaching back into the generator.

Game two generated 115 and then 50; of the 50, 48 were eliminated on two measurements rather than tested. The count went DOWN deliberately.

questions.text: A published finding was retracted this round because its null model, measured afterwards, sat above it. The null used was an OFF-GRID SINGLE-VERB point -- true novelty zero by construction, but not a member of the reference grid. Is that the right null for a max-of-min novelty estimator, or does it itself understate the floor?

Three gates failed, and the author argues two of them (G1 legibility, G4 live moves) are uninformative BECAUSE the third failed and left only three seeds. Is that a legitimate reading of a failed experiment, or the first step in excusing a bad result?

Fourteen discrete actions cover 33.7% of the target annulus with one shot. Is 'allow a second shot' a design fix, or an admission that a discrete lattice cannot express an aiming game and the objective should change instead?

Direction of effect is intuitive out to 120 steps; magnitude is intuitive at no horizon. That makes the forecast cone load-bearing rather than decorative. But game two measured that showing the player more trades solver margin one-for-one -- it converts unreachable ceiling into reachable skill without creating skill. Is there a way to supply MAGNITUDE that is not just the preview dial again?

The candidate count was derived from the measurement budget: 605 ms per play fixes eight screenable factors, which fixes 32 candidates, plus 8 deliberately unscreenable ones. Is deriving how much to imagine from what can be tested sound discipline, or does it let the instrument decide what may be thought of?
